name: Ratnamala Swain / ରତ୍ନମାଳା ସ୍ବାଇଁ

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Ratnamala Swain combines architecture with poetry, editing and translation in Odia. She edited the literary magazine Chitra from 1993 to 2010, and her collections include Diary Kabita, Naeera Ghara and Photoframe. With Purabi Das, she translated Sitadevi Khadanga’s Jibansmruti into English for Sahitya Akademi. Her own poetry appears in English in Claiming the Sky, translated by Purabi Das and Durga Prasad Panda and published by Dhauli Books.

In “ଧଉଳି ପାହାଡ”, a visit to Dhauli becomes a conversation with an apparently sleeping Buddha. Vendors, photographers, tourists and monkeys occupy the foreground, while the hill bears witness to the poem’s remembered violence and transformation. The speaker is drawn to the road as much as the monument, returning with questions while choosing to remain within the everyday world. The poem holds historical memory, restlessness and spiritual questioning in the same landscape.
